title: the indexer's groupings
line: a census page focused on a household member, the relatives its tables group around him FamilySearch's own: once the owner accepts the son, the father is taken through the son's own stated relationship to the head, while the mother is not taken through the Parents and Siblings table, the brother nobody fits is not created, and the decision on the mother writes the couple undecided, saying the record's indexer states it; on the head's own page the same kind of row is the census's own column, stated: once the owner accepts the head, his wife is taken through it and his son and daughter, whom nobody fits, are created, each placed under him alone: the census states them his and her his wife, never their mother, so they never join the couple's family beside a wife the record does not name as their mother

steps.say: the 1950 household's page, found through the son's own search and saved by hand: read and matched for the son

expect.why: the son alone is proposed; the household waits on him

steps.say: the son accepted by the owner: his own field states his relationship to the head, the Parents and Siblings table is FamilySearch's

expect.why: the son's relationship to the head is the census's own statement: the father is taken through it, the tree claiming the link

why.has: its indexer's, not the record's own statement

expect.why: the mother is related on the page only by FamilySearch's Parents and Siblings table: the claimed route does not take her
the mother, put to the tree's own mother, is a card for the owner

why.has: the record's indexer, not the record, relates them to a person accepted on it (Brother)

expect.why: the rule creates a person only on a relationship the record states
a brother the table groups under the son, whom nobody fits, is a card for the owner

steps.say: the owner accepts the mother on it: the couple written undecided, the indexer's grouping

expect.why: FamilySearch's table computes the couple: written undecided, never an accepted family link

note.has: written undecided: the record's indexer, not the record, states it

steps.say: the 1900 household's page, the head's own: two cards, the head and his wife

expect.why: the head and the wife the tree holds; the mother, the son and the daughter wait on the head

steps.say: the head accepted by the owner: on his own page the tables are worded from his side, each row's word is the census's own column

expect.why: the wife's row is her relationship to the head, stated: the claimed route takes her
a son the census states, whom nobody fits, is created by the rule
the son and the daughter created
the census states her the head's daughter and Lena the head's wife, never Lena her mother: she is placed under him alone, not in the couple's family
and her brother beside her, in the one family of his alone

the couple stands on the census, yet no family joins her to the wife on the record's word
